translations.answer: The original thread's maintainer/author responded that MJX does not support directly stacking heterogeneous models. An alternative direction is to host-side dispatch, or pre-load the maximum number of objects, and then move unused objects out of the workspace while keeping their positions fixed. However, the reply explicitly states that this is not a verified workaround and is only a bounded fix. The max_contact_points/max_geom_pairs can only save some collision detection, but does not eliminate other JAX engine operations. Therefore, this is a pending testable bounded fix, not a verified variable-length model support.
translations.applicability: This is applicable to MJX environments that can tolerate fixed maximum model shape, additional object overhead, and position mask risk. The position change of static world objects has a separate recompilation boundary.
translations.credibility.rationale: No reproducible records have been formed yet.
translations.details.attempts.0: The maintainer suggests randomizing the positions of movable objects during environment reset.
translations.details.attempts.1: The maintainer points to domain randomization in mjx.Model.geom_size for primitive sizes.
translations.details.attempts.2: The reply suggests host dispatch for different object counts, or pre-loading the maximum number and moving unused objects out of the workspace.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First, determine whether the randomization is per environment state (e.g., movable object qpos), model parameters (e.g., geom_size), or pre-compile topology/static world geometry.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Check if the JAX pytree shape of heterogeneous models is consistent, not just the structural names.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Randomize movable object positions during environment reset, rather than rebuilding the model for each position.
translations.details.environments.0: Issue #1684, 2024–2026 replies; JAX static shape and batch models.
translations.details.limits.0: The maintainer states that mesh size/shape randomization is more difficult.
translations.details.limits.1: The reply for loading all meshes and removing unused objects is explicitly marked as not attempted/YMMV.
translations.details.limits.2: max_contact_points/max_geom_pairs can save some collision detection work, but the reply explicitly states it does not eliminate other JAX engine work.
translations.details.limits.3: The original thread did not confirm that all geom_size changes in the new version are unnecessary to set_const/compile again, so this is not pushed forward.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The maintainer provides a division of position/data interfaces for movable objects.
translations.details.outcomes.1: There is no official direct support for different mesh/object counts in a single MJX batch; mask schemes have not been validated in the original thread.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Where should movable object positions and primitive sizes be randomized in MJX?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How can one support different object counts or mesh shapes in a single MJX batch?
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: MJX does not support directly stacking heterogeneous models with different shapes.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The JAX static shape prevents different counts of objects from being freely variable in a single compiled batch.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The user is unsure whether to modify mjx.Model or mjx.Data during environment reset.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Different shape/object count models cannot be directly stacked into the same MJX batch.
translations.details.symptoms.2: A static world object, if changed position during reset, will trigger a recompilation in the thread reply.
